ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: Life Is a Journey to Be Experienced

fullPassage:
Hi, everyone. My name is Minji Song, and I am the editor of an online teen magazine, Teens Today. I am honored to have been asked to give a talk. Many of our high school student subscribers send me messages with concerns about their future. So today, I will talk about the value of experiences in making a better future. For this talk, I asked my old friends to write down stories about what they experienced when they were younger. I would like to start by reading them one by one.

I was fond of swimming
One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist looked fantastic, and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They approved and said, "Yes." Swimming was difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer. I felt tired but happy when I was out of breath after every practice. As I practiced more, my times got better and better. One day, my coach suggested that I enter a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training. The training was demanding, leaving me exhausted at times. Whenever I felt this way, I told myself, "No pain, no gain."

I performed in a play
I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do it. I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more confident. On the day of the performance, I got anxious and my mind went blank just before I stepped on the stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and encouraged me. Thanks to this, I was able to perform my lines perfectly.

I wanted to be a landscape architect
One day, I saw a poster advertising the city's landscape design contest. The instant I saw it, I got interested. After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was impressive because the arrangement of plants and structures can transform a space. This inspired me to think about becoming a landscape architect. I found out that I had to be good at math and science in order to become a landscape architect. This is because landscape architects must calculate the dimensions and slopes of land as well as thoroughly examine environmental factors such as soil, air, and climate. I was not good at either subject at the time, so I decided to put more effort into studying them.

I was passionate about writing
When I was fourteen, I was hospitalized for several weeks. One day, I saw a piece of paper on the table. I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time. I felt a sense of relief when I wrote what I wanted to do after leaving the hospital. That evening, I asked my mother to buy me a notebook. As I filled page after page, I realized that writing was more than just a way to kill time. As the years passed, my passion for writing grew stronger. So I started writing short stories and sharing them with my friends and family. I felt a sense of accomplishment whenever they told me my stories were good.

Can you guess what my friends do now? Are they a swimmer? An actor? A landscape architect? A novelist? Actually, all four of these people are me! I currently work as a magazine editor. As you can see, my preferences have changed over the years as I was exposed to new experiences. Every time my interest changed, I was worried about what I was going to become in the future. Do you also have similar concerns?

Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed writing. Thanks to these many interests, I can write articles about math and science, speak confidently in front of an audience, and relieve my stress by swimming.

Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time. Your school days are a time of self-discovery and personal growth. As you spend each day wisely, you will be able to figure out what kind of person you are and what you enjoy doing. Do not attempt to define yourself in just one way as you undergo this process. Be flexible. Remember that your potential is limitless.

Thank you for your time.

questions.passage: Hi, everyone. My name is Minji Song, and I am the editor of an online teen magazine, Teens Today. I am (A)[honored / ashamed] to have been asked to give a talk. Many of our high school student subscribers send me messages with (B)[concerns / satisfaction] about their future. So today, I will talk about the value of (C)[experiences / theories] in making a better future. For this talk, I asked my old friends to write down stories about what they experienced when they were younger.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 강연을 요청받게 되어 영광(honored)이다. 학생들이 미래에 대한 걱정(concerns)을 담은 메시지를 보낸다. 경험(experiences)의 가치에 관해 이야기하겠다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② honored — concerns — experiences: 원문 일치. 강연 요청에 영광, 미래 걱정, 경험의 가치.
❌ ① ashamed(부끄러운): honored의 반의어. 강연 요청에 부끄러움은 문맥상 부적절.
❌ ③ satisfaction(만족): concerns의 반의어. 미래에 대해 만족을 담은 메시지는 어색.
❌ ④ theories(이론): experiences의 대조 개념. 글의 주제는 경험의 가치.
det.tip: honored(영광스러운) ↔ ashamed(부끄러운), concerns(걱정) ↔ satisfaction(만족), experiences(경험) ↔ theories(이론)

questions.passage: One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist looked (A)[fantastic / terrible], and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They (B)[approved / rejected] and said, "Yes." Swimming was difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer. The training was (C)[demanding / effortless], leaving me exhausted at times.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 금메달리스트가 대단해(fantastic) 보였다. 부모님이 허락(approved)하셨다. 훈련은 힘들었고(demanding) 지치게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ fantastic — approved — demanding: 원문 일치.
❌ ① effortless(수월한): demanding의 반의어. 'exhausted(지친)'와 모순.
❌ ② rejected(거부한): approved의 반의어. 'Yes'라고 말했으므로 거부가 아님.
❌ ③ terrible(끔찍한): fantastic의 반의어. 금메달리스트를 보고 닮고 싶었으므로 부적절.
det.tip: fantastic(대단한) ↔ terrible(끔찍한), approved(허락한) ↔ rejected(거부한), demanding(힘든) ↔ effortless(수월한)

questions.passage: After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was (A)[impressive / negligible] because the arrangement of plants and structures can (B)[transform / preserve] a space. This (C)[inspired / discouraged] me to think about becoming a landscape architect. I found out that I had to be good at math and science in order to become a landscape architect. I was not good at either subject at the time, so I decided to put more effort into studying them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 조경 건축가의 일이 인상적(impressive)이라고 생각했다. 식물과 구조물 배열로 공간을 변화시킬(transform) 수 있기 때문. 이것이 조경 건축가가 되는 것에 대해 생각하도록 영감을 주었다(inspired).
det.analysis:
✅ ① impressive — transform — inspired: 원문 일치.
❌ ② negligible(무시할 만한): impressive의 반의어. '인상적'이어야 조경 건축가를 꿈꾸게 됨.
❌ ③ preserve(보존하다): transform의 대조 개념. '변화시킬 수 있기 때문에 인상적'이라는 문맥.
❌ ④ discouraged(낙담시키다): inspired의 반의어. 인상적인 일에 영감을 받았으므로 낙담은 모순.
det.tip: impressive(인상적인) ↔ negligible(무시할 만한), transform(변화시키다) ↔ preserve(보존하다), inspired(영감을 주다) ↔ discouraged(낙담시키다)

questions.passage: I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. I was so ①<u>nervous</u> at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more ②<u>confident</u>. On the day of the performance, I got ③<u>relaxed</u> and my mind went blank just before I stepped on the stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and ④<u>encouraged</u> me.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 공연 당일 무대에 오르기 직전에 ③편안했다(relaxed)고 했는데, 정신이 멍해졌다(mind went blank)는 것과 모순. 원문: anxious(불안한)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ relaxed → anxious: '정신이 멍해졌다'는 불안감의 결과. 편안했다면 멍해지지 않음.
❌ ① nervous(긴장한): 첫 예행연습에서 대사를 전혀 못했으므로 적절.
❌ ② confident(자신감 있는): 연습할수록 자신감이 생겼으므로 적절.
❌ ④ encouraged(격려하다): 반 친구들이 어깨를 두드리며 격려했으므로 적절.
det.tip: anxious(불안한) ↔ relaxed(편안한). 'mind went blank(머릿속이 하얘지다)'는 불안/긴장의 표현.

questions.passage: When I was fourteen, I was hospitalized for several weeks. One day, I saw a piece of paper on the table. I was ①<u>bored</u>, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time. I felt a sense of ②<u>anxiety</u> when I wrote what I wanted to do after leaving the hospital. As I filled page after page, I realized that writing was more than just a way to ③<u>kill</u> time. As the years passed, my ④<u>passion</u> for writing grew stronger.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 퇴원 후 하고 싶은 것을 적었을 때 ②불안감(anxiety)을 느꼈다고 했는데, 원문: relief(안도감). 하고 싶은 것을 적으면서 느끼는 감정은 안도감이 자연스럽다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② anxiety → relief: 퇴원 후 계획을 적으면서 느끼는 감정은 '안도감'이지 '불안감'이 아님.
❌ ① bored(지루한): 입원 중 지루했으므로 적절.
❌ ③ kill(때우다): 'kill time(시간을 때우다)'는 관용표현으로 적절.
❌ ④ passion(열정): 글쓰기에 대한 열정이 커졌으므로 적절.
det.tip: relief(안도감) ↔ anxiety(불안감). 'a sense of relief(안도감)'은 걱정이 해소될 때 쓰는 표현.

questions.passage: One day, I saw a poster advertising the city's landscape design contest. After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves ①<u>arranging</u> and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was impressive because the arrangement of plants and structures can transform a space. I found out that I had to be good at math and science in order to become a landscape architect. This is because landscape architects must calculate the ②<u>dimensions</u> and ③<u>slopes</u> of land as well as ④<u>superficially</u> examine environmental factors such as soil, air, and climate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 환경 요소를 ④피상적으로(superficially) 조사한다고 했는데, 원문: thoroughly(철저히). 조경 건축가는 환경 요소를 철저히 조사해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ superficially → thoroughly: 전문가가 환경 요소를 '피상적으로' 조사하는 것은 부적절. '철저히' 조사해야 함.
❌ ① arranging(배열하다): 조경 디자인이 외부 공간을 배열하고 꾸미는 일이므로 적절.
❌ ② dimensions(넓이/치수): 땅의 넓이를 계산하는 것이므로 적절.
❌ ③ slopes(경사/기울기): 땅의 기울기를 계산하는 것이므로 적절.
det.tip: thoroughly(철저히) ↔ superficially(피상적으로). 'as well as(~뿐만 아니라)'로 연결되어 calculate과 examine 모두 전문적 역량.

questions.passage: One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist looked fantastic, and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They __________ and said, "Yes." Swimming was difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 부모님이 수영을 배워도 되냐고 물었더니 'Yes'라고 말씀하셨으므로 허락(approved)하신 것.
det.analysis:
✅ ① approved(허락하다): 'said "Yes"'에서 허락한 것임을 알 수 있음.
❌ ② rejected(거부하다): 'Yes'라고 했으므로 거부가 아님.
❌ ③ hesitated(망설이다): 'Yes'라고 바로 답했으므로 망설임이 아님.
❌ ④ complained(불평하다): 불평했다면 'Yes'라고 말하지 않을 것.
det.tip: approve(승인/허락하다): 동의나 허가를 나타낼 때 사용. approve of + 명사 = ~을 찬성하다.

questions.passage: I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do it. I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 처음에 긴장해서 대사를 전혀 못했지만, 연습할수록 점점 더 자신감(confident)이 생겼다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ confident(자신감 있는): 'However'로 전환, 연습 후 긴장→자신감 변화.
❌ ① anxious(불안한): nervous와 유사어. However 역접 후 반대 감정이 와야 함.
❌ ② doubtful(의심스러운): 연습 효과가 부정적이 되어 문맥 불일치.
❌ ④ indifferent(무관심한): 연습을 계속했으므로 무관심하지 않음.
det.tip: confident(자신감 있는) ↔ nervous/anxious(긴장한/불안한). 'more and more + 형용사' = 점점 더 ~한.

questions.passage: Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to __________ experiences which will help shape your future. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed writing. Thanks to these many interests, I can write articles about math and science, speak confidently in front of an audience, and relieve my stress by swimming.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새로운 것을 탐구하면 미래를 만드는 데 도움이 될 귀중한(valuable) 경험으로 이어질 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② valuable(귀중한): 'help shape your future(미래를 만드는 데 도움)'이므로 귀중한 경험.
❌ ① ordinary(평범한): 미래를 만드는 데 도움이 될 경험이 '평범한'이면 의미가 약함.
❌ ③ harmful(해로운): 긍정적 맥락에서 '해로운 경험'은 부적절.
❌ ④ trivial(하찮은): 미래에 도움이 되는 경험을 '하찮다'고 하는 것은 모순.
det.tip: valuable(귀중한) ↔ trivial(하찮은). 'lead to + 명사' = ~으로 이어지다.

questions.passage: One day, my coach suggested that I enter a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training. The training was <u>demanding</u>, leaving me exhausted at times. Whenever I felt this way, I told myself, "No pain, no gain."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 demanding의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 훈련은 힘들었고(demanding), 때로는 지치게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ challenging(도전적인/힘든): demanding과 동의어. 둘 다 많은 노력을 요구한다는 뜻.
❌ ① effortless(수월한): demanding의 반의어.
❌ ② relaxing(편안한): demanding의 반의어.
❌ ③ simple(간단한): demanding의 반의어.
det.tip: demanding = challenging = tough = strenuous (힘든, 고된). 'exhausted(지친)'가 단서.

questions.passage: After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was <u>impressive</u> because the arrangement of plants and structures can transform a space. This inspired me to think about becoming a landscape architect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 impressive의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 조경 건축가의 일이 인상적(impressive)이라고 생각했다. 공간을 변화시킬 수 있기 때문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① remarkable(주목할 만한): impressive와 동의어. 둘 다 깊은 인상을 준다는 뜻.
❌ ② ordinary(평범한): impressive의 반의어.
❌ ③ disappointing(실망스러운): impressive의 반의어.
❌ ④ insignificant(하찮은): impressive의 반의어.
det.tip: impressive = remarkable = striking = outstanding (인상적인). 'inspired(영감을 주다)'가 인상적이었음의 결과.

questions.passage: Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time. Your school days are a time of self-discovery and personal growth. As you spend each day wisely, you will be able to <u>figure out</u> what kind of person you are and what you enjoy doing.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 figure out의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 하루하루를 현명하게 보내면 어떤 사람인지 알아낼(figure out) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ determine(알아내다/결정하다): figure out과 동의어. 정보를 찾아내거나 이해한다는 뜻.
❌ ① overlook(간과하다): 알아내기와 반대.
❌ ② ignore(무시하다): 알아내기와 반대.
❌ ④ complicate(복잡하게 하다): 알아내기와 무관.
det.tip: figure out = determine = find out = work out (알아내다). 구동사(phrasal verb) 형태에 주의.

questions.passage: I used to be quiet and <u>shy</u> when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 shy의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: 어릴 때 조용하고 수줍은(shy) 성격이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② outgoing(외향적인): shy의 반의어. 사교적이고 적극적인 성격.
❌ ① timid(소심한): shy와 동의어.
❌ ③ reserved(내성적인): shy와 유사어.
❌ ④ withdrawn(움츠린): shy와 유사어.
det.tip: shy(수줍은) = timid = reserved ↔ outgoing(외향적인) = sociable = extroverted.

questions.passage: Do not attempt to define yourself in just one way as you undergo this process. Be <u>flexible</u>. Remember that your potential is limitless. Thank you for your time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 flexible의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: 유연(flexible)해지라. 잠재력은 무한하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ rigid(완고한/경직된): flexible의 반의어.
❌ ① adaptable(적응력 있는): flexible과 동의어.
❌ ② versatile(다재다능한): flexible과 유사어.
❌ ③ elastic(탄력 있는): flexible과 유사어.
det.tip: flexible(유연한) = adaptable = versatile ↔ rigid(경직된) = inflexible = stubborn.

questions.passage:
(A) I found out that I had to be good at math and science in order to become a landscape architect. I was not good at either <u>subject</u> at the time, so I decided to put more effort into studying them.

(B) The <u>subject</u> of today's lecture is the impact of technology on education. Many students found it very informative.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 subject의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 수학과 과학 두 과목(subject) 모두 잘하지 못했다. (B) 오늘 강의의 주제(subject)는 기술이 교육에 미치는 영향이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 과목 — 주제: (A)는 math and science를 가리키므로 '과목', (B)는 강의 내용이므로 '주제'.
❌ ② 주제 — 과목: (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜.
❌ ③ 주제 — 주제: (A)는 '과목'이 맞음.
❌ ④ 과목 — 과목: (B)는 '주제'가 맞음.
det.tip: subject 다의어: ① 과목(school subject) ② 주제(topic/theme) ③ 대상(subject of experiment). 문맥에서 판단.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who regularly receives a newspaper, magazine, or similar publication"

det.korean: 신문, 잡지 등을 정기적으로 받는 사람 = 구독자(subscriber)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ subscriber(구독자): 정기적으로 출판물을 받는 사람.
❌ ① publisher(출판사/발행인): 출판물을 만드는 사람.
❌ ② editor(편집자): 출판물을 편집하는 사람.
❌ ④ advertiser(광고주): 광고를 내는 사람.
det.tip: subscribe(구독하다) → subscriber(구독자) → subscription(구독). 본문의 'subscribers send me messages'에서 등장.

questions.passage: He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training. The training was demanding, leaving me __________ (exhaust) at times.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 훈련은 힘들었고, 때로는 나를 지치게(exhausted) 했다.
det.analysis: leaving me exhausted: 분사구문에서 me를 보충 설명하는 과거분사. '나를 지치게 만들며'라는 의미로, exhaust → exhausted (과거분사/형용사).
det.tip: exhaust(v. 지치게 하다) → exhausted(adj. 지친) → exhausting(adj. 지치게 하는). 'leaving + 목적어 + 분사' 구문에서 목적어의 상태를 나타냄.

questions.passage: The instant I saw it, I got interested. After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and __________ (decorate) outdoor spaces.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 조경 디자인이 외부 공간을 배열하고 꾸미는(decorating) 일을 포함한다.
det.analysis: involves arranging and decorating: 'involve + 동명사' 구문. and로 arranging과 병렬 연결되므로 decorate → decorating.
det.tip: involve + V-ing(동명사): ~을 수반하다/포함하다. 병렬 구조에서 and 앞뒤 동일 형태 유지.

questions.passage: I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more confident. On the day of the performance, I got anxious and my mind __________ just before I stepped on the stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and encouraged me. Thanks to this, I was able to perform my lines perfectly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 공연 당일 무대에 오르기 직전에 불안했고 정신이 멍해졌다(went blank).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ went blank(멍해지다): anxious(불안한) + 무대 직전이라는 상황과 일치. 긴장으로 머릿속이 하얘지는 것.
❌ ① lit up(밝아지다): 긍정적 표현. anxious와 모순.
❌ ② became clear(명확해지다): 불안한 상태와 모순.
❌ ④ turned sharp(예리해지다): anxious와 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: go blank = 멍해지다/하얘지다. 'My mind went blank'은 긴장이나 충격으로 아무 생각이 나지 않는 상태를 표현하는 관용구.

questions.passage: Can you guess what my friends do now? Actually, all four of these people are me! I currently work as a magazine editor. As you can see, my preferences have changed over the years as I was __________ new experiences. Every time my interest changed, I was worried about what I was going to become in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새로운 경험에 노출되면서(exposed to) 좋아하는 것들이 수년간 바뀌어 왔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ exposed to(~에 노출되다): 새로운 경험에 노출됨에 따라 선호도가 변했다는 맥락과 일치.
❌ ① limited by(~에 제한되다): 선호도 변화와 어울리지 않음.
❌ ② afraid of(~을 두려워하다): 새로운 경험을 두려워했다면 선호도가 변하지 않았을 것.
❌ ③ bored with(~에 지루해하다): 부정적 뉘앙스. 글의 전체 주제(경험의 가치)와 모순.
det.tip: be exposed to = ~에 노출되다. expose(v.) → exposed(adj.) → exposure(n.). 본문에서 경험의 가치를 강조하는 핵심 표현.
